transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, it may not be a big thing, doctor, but I’ve been having trouble when I get into certain tight places… like a slow elevator or a little locked room. My chest sort of jumps right away, and I get this strong feeling like I need to get back out before I can even think straight. I wasn’t sure if that’s the kind of thing I should come in for.
Does this fear happen only when you’re in enclosed spaces?

Yes, mostly just those kinds of places. I mean, I know a little storage room or an elevator at the museum isn’t really the same as being locked up or anything serious… but when there’s no window and the door shuts tight, my mind kind of treats it like trouble right away. Does that make sense?
Do these sudden rushes of fear ever happen when you’re not in a tight or enclosed space?

No, not really, doctor. It’s pretty much when I’m in—or even about to be in—some tight place like a small storage room or an elevator. I know it’s not actually like being locked up or anything, but if there’s no window and that door shuts tight, my mind just treats it like trouble right away.
Do you also get this fear in open public places where getting out might be hard, like being in a crowd or on a bus?
I don’t think so, doctor. Crowds or a bus don’t really stand out to me that way. It’s more the closed-in sort of places I was talking about. I hope I’m explaining that right.
